items.title: Linearly realized Standard Model EFT field and scale data
items.design_state: Adopts the linearly realized three-family Standard Model field and gauge data and a finite B- and L-conserving canonical-dimension-six local model, with explicit scales and physical limits.
items.statement:
Adopt four-dimensional affine Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with coordinates $x^0=ct$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ for engineering dimensions, so $\partial_\mu$ has mass dimension one, a scalar field has dimension one, a spinor field has dimension $3/2$, and a gauge field strength has dimension two.

The gauge group is the direct product $G_{\mathrm{SM}}=SU(3)_c\times SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$, with this global form and not a quotient by a subgroup of its center. Write an element of $U(1)_Y$ as $z\in U(1)$ and normalize its integer charge as $y=6Y$, so its representation acts by $z^y$. The three-family matter fields and scalar are smooth fields in the representations
$$q_L:(3,2)_1,\qquad u_R:(3,1)_4,\qquad d_R:(3,1)_{-2},\qquad \ell_L:(1,2)_{-3},\qquad e_R:(1,1)_{-6},\qquad H:(1,2)_3.$$
There are no right-handed neutrino fields. Fix the finite Grassmann coefficient algebra $\mathcal G=\Lambda_{\mathbb C}(\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_N)$ for some finite $N\geq1$, graded by exterior parity, with the conjugate-linear involution $\zeta_a^\dagger=\zeta_a$ and $(uv)^\dagger=v^\dagger u^\dagger$. On the trivial spin structure of $M$, use the spinor space $S=\mathbb C^4$ with matrices $\gamma^\mu\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(S)$ satisfying
$$\gamma^\mu\gamma^\nu+\gamma^\nu\gamma^\mu=2\eta^{\mu\nu}I,\qquad (\gamma^0)^\dagger=-\gamma^0,\qquad (\gamma^j)^\dagger=\gamma^j\quad (j=1,2,3).$$
Set $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$, $P_L=(I-\gamma_5)/2$, and $P_R=(I+\gamma_5)/2$. Thus the left- and right-handed Weyl spaces are $S_L=P_LS$ and $S_R=P_RS$; the infinitesimal Lorentz spin action on $S$ is generated by $\mathsf S^{\mu\nu}=\tfrac14[\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu]$. For a spinor field define its Dirac adjoint by $\bar\psi=\psi^\dagger i\gamma^0$, with conjugation also acting on its internal and Grassmann components. The fermion components take values in $\mathcal G_{\bar1}$, while $H$ is a Grassmann-even complex doublet. The global charges are $B(q_L)=B(u_R)=B(d_R)=1/3$, $L(\ell_L)=L(e_R)=1$, and zero for $H$ and the gauge fields; the corresponding $U(1)_B$ and $U(1)_L$ transformations multiply each field by the phase determined by its charge. Impose these as exact selection rules on the retained formal local interactions; no anomaly-free quantum-current claim is made. There is no flavor symmetry beyond the displayed gauge action: Yukawa and Wilson coefficients may carry unrestricted three-family indices subject to the stated reality and Hermitian-conjugation conditions.

Here $\mathbf 3=\mathbb C^3$ and $\mathbf 2=\mathbb C^2$ are the defining representations of $SU(3)_c$ and $SU(2)_L$, respectively, and $\mathbf 1$ is the trivial representation. The family space $\mathbb C^3_{\!f}$ has trivial gauge action. In the order displayed above, the internal family-and-gauge carriers are $\mathbb C^3_{\!f}\otimes\mathbb C^3\otimes\mathbb C^2$, $\mathbb C^3_{\!f}\otimes\mathbb C^3$, $\mathbb C^3_{\!f}\otimes\mathbb C^3$, $\mathbb C^3_{\!f}\otimes\mathbb C^2$, $\mathbb C^3_{\!f}$, and $\mathbb C^2$. On these carriers the element $(g_3,g_2,z)\in G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ acts by
$$\rho_{q_L}=z\,(I_f\otimes g_3\otimes g_2),\quad \rho_{u_R}=z^4(I_f\otimes g_3),\quad \rho_{d_R}=z^{-2}(I_f\otimes g_3),\quad \rho_{\ell_L}=z^{-3}(I_f\otimes g_2),\quad \rho_{e_R}=z^{-6}I_f,\quad \rho_H=z^3g_2,$$
where $I_f$ is the identity on $\mathbb C^3_{\!f}$ and omitted group factors act trivially. The listed carriers are the internal factors; the matter fields, including their spacetime spin type, are the smooth maps
$$\begin{aligned}  q_L&:M\to\mathcal G_{\bar1}\otimes S_L\otimes\mathbb C^3_{\!f}\otimes\mathbb C^3\otimes\mathbb C^2,& u_R,d_R&:M\to\mathcal G_{\bar1}\otimes S_R\otimes\mathbb C^3_{\!f}\otimes\mathbb C^3,\\ \ell_L&:M\to\mathcal G_{\bar1}\otimes S_L\otimes\mathbb C^3_{\!f}\otimes\mathbb C^2,& e_R&:M\to\mathcal G_{\bar1}\otimes S_R\otimes\mathbb C^3_{\!f},& H&:M\to\mathbb C^2 . \end{aligned}$$
Each Grassmann coefficient function is smooth on $M$; the Lorentz spin action is on $S_{L/R}$ and the displayed gauge action is on the internal factors.

Choose a reference radius $v>0$ of mass dimension one; it denotes a vacuum radius only under the optional full-potential condition below. Define
$$\sigma^1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma^2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma^3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad T^I=\frac{\sigma^I}{2},$$
and $\widetilde H=i\sigma^2H^*$.

Choose the trivial smooth right principal bundle $P=M\times G_{\mathrm{SM}}$ and only this bundle sector. A connection is a smooth right-principal connection with the convention $\omega(Z_P)=Z$ and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$. In a local section write its form as $A=A_\mu dx^\mu$. Choose Hermitian generators $t^A$ for the defining $SU(3)_c$ representation with $\operatorname{tr}(t^At^B)=\delta^{AB}/2$ and $[t^A,t^B]=if^{ABC}t^C$; the $T^I$ satisfy $[T^I,T^J]=i\epsilon^{IJK}T^K$, with $\epsilon^{123}=1$. Let $G^A=G_\mu^A dx^\mu$, $W^I=W_\mu^I dx^\mu$, and $B=B_\mu dx^\mu$ be smooth real gauge-potential one-forms with components of mass dimension one, and take $g_s,g,g'>0$ dimensionless. In the product Lie algebra, the local connection components are $(ig_sG_\mu^At^A,\;igW_\mu^IT^I,\;ig'B_\mu/6)$, where the final entry uses the generator $i$ of $\mathfrak u(1)$ for the coordinate $z=e^{i\vartheta}$. Thus in a charge-$y$ representation
$$\rho_*(A_\mu)=ig_sG_\mu^At^A+igW_\mu^IT^I+ig'B_\mu Y,\qquad Y=y/6,$$
with absent factors acting as zero. A field in representation $\rho$ has $D_\mu=\partial_\mu+\rho_*(A_\mu)$; this acts trivially on its Lorentz spin factor in the global flat frame. In particular $D_\mu H=\partial_\mu H+igW_\mu^IT^IH+\tfrac{i}{2}g'B_\mu H$. Define the curvature components by
$$G_{\mu\nu}^A=\partial_\mu G_\nu^A-\partial_\nu G_\mu^A-g_sf^{ABC}G_\mu^BG_\nu^C,\quad W_{\mu\nu}^I=\partial_\mu W_\nu^I-\partial_\nu W_\mu^I-g\epsilon^{IJK}W_\mu^JW_\nu^K,\quad B_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu B_\nu-\partial_\nu B_\mu;$$
they are the coefficients of $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$ under the supplied graded-bracket convention. The representation differential and gauge couplings are dimensionless, so $A_\mu$ has mass dimension one. The ordinary component hypercharges are $Y=y/6$; in particular $Y(H)=1/2$. The formal local interaction set imposes the exact $U(1)_B$ and $U(1)_L$ selection rules stated above; no anomaly-free quantum-current claim is made. Yukawa matrices are otherwise arbitrary.

The adopted object is a formal local Lagrangian density made from finitely many fields, covariant derivatives, and field strengths at one spacetime point, contracted to Lorentz scalars and invariant under the stated gauge and global actions. The renormalizable part has the gauge kinetic terms $-\tfrac14G^A_{\mu\nu}G^{A\mu\nu}-\tfrac14W^I_{\mu\nu}W^{I\mu\nu}-\tfrac14B_{\mu\nu}B^{\mu\nu}$, fermion kinetic terms $-\sum_\psi\bar\psi\gamma^\mu D_\mu\psi$, Higgs kinetic term $-(D_\mu H)^\dagger D^\mu H$, and potential contribution $-V_4(H)$, where the real gauge-invariant potential is
$$V_4(H)=V_0-\mu_H^2H^\dagger H+\lambda(H^\dagger H)^2,\qquad V_0,\mu_H^2,\lambda\in\mathbb R,$$
and Yukawa terms
$$-\left(\bar q_LY_dHd_R+\bar q_LY_u\widetilde H u_R+\bar\ell_LY_eHe_R+\mathrm{h.c.}\right),$$
where each $Y_f$ is a complex $3\times3$ family matrix and h.c. is the Hermitian conjugate. With the stated Clifford and adjoint conventions the kinetic prefactor is $-1$: writing $B_S=i\gamma^0$, one has $(B_S\gamma^\mu)^\dagger=-B_S\gamma^\mu$, so $\int\bar\psi\gamma^\mu D_\mu\psi$ is Hermitian after integration by parts under the stated boundary convention. Equivalently the density may be replaced by $-\tfrac12[\bar\psi\gamma^\mu D_\mu\psi-(D_\mu\bar\psi)\gamma^\mu\psi]$, where $D_\mu\bar\psi=\partial_\mu\bar\psi-\bar\psi\rho_*(A_\mu)$. For translating source four-component spinor factors from the mostly-minus metric, use $\eta_{\mathrm{src}}=-\eta$, $\Gamma^\mu=-i\gamma^\mu$ and $\bar\psi_{\mathrm{src}}=\psi^\dagger\Gamma^0=-\bar\psi$, with $\Gamma_5=i\Gamma^0\Gamma^1\Gamma^2\Gamma^3=\gamma_5$; source spinor factors are read with this explicit change of conventions. Scalar and gauge contractions use the explicit local conventions, including the separately specified Warsaw scalar representatives; numerical source coefficients require the corresponding convention conversion before identification. In particular $i\bar\psi_{\mathrm{src}}\Gamma^\mu D_\mu\psi=-\bar\psi\gamma^\mu D_\mu\psi$. Set the gauge theta terms to zero in this selected model. Add finite sets $I_d$ of local gauge-invariant, $B$- and $L$-neutral polynomial operators $\mathcal O_{d,i}$ at each retained dimension $d\leq6$. Retain derivative-jet order at most two, maximum polynomial field degree six, and loop order zero. Use $C_{d,i}\mathcal O_{d,i}/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^{d-4}$, where $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ has mass dimension one and each $C_{d,i}$ is dimensionless. The dimension-five set is empty under the adopted exact lepton-number symmetry. The dimension-six set is fixed by the separate Warsaw coefficient contract. Wilson coefficients are supplied parameters, not calculated or fitted here.

In these natural units $Y_f$ has mass dimension zero, $V_0$ has dimension four, $\mu_H^2$ has dimension two, and $\lambda$ has dimension zero; the Lagrangian density has mass dimension four. To define the retained scalar potential, set $s=H^\dagger H\geq0$ and evaluate the full retained Lagrangian on constant $H$, with fermions, gauge fields and all derivatives set to zero. Let $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{add}}^{(0)}(s)$ be the sum of all retained operator contributions surviving this evaluation, including their Wilson coefficients, powers of $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$, and the Hermitian-conjugate terms required for a real density, each counted as in the adopted Lagrangian. Define
$$\left.\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ret}}\right|_{\mathrm{constant}\ H,\,\mathrm{others}=0}=-V_{\mathrm{ret}}(s),\qquad V_{\mathrm{ret}}(s)=V_4(s)-\mathcal L_{\mathrm{add}}^{(0)}(s).$$
In the dimension-six Warsaw scalar-potential sector, $Q_H=(H^\dagger H)^3$ has real coefficient $C_H$ and Lagrangian contribution $+C_Hs^3/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2$, hence contributes $-C_Hs^3/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2$ to $V_{\mathrm{ret}}$. The derivative operators $Q_{H\Box}$ and $Q_{HD}$ vanish in this constant-field evaluation. In particular, when the only addition to $V_4$ is this Warsaw potential term,
$$V_{\mathrm{ret}}(s)=V_0-\mu_H^2s+\lambda s^2-\frac{C_H}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}s^3.$$

The optional interpretation of $v$ as a vacuum radius assumes that $s_v=v^2/2>0$ is a local minimum of this full $V_{\mathrm{ret}}$ within the field range where the truncated EFT is being used. Thus $V_{\mathrm{ret}}'(s_v)=0$ is necessary. If a nondegenerate radial minimum is selected, impose also $V_{\mathrm{ret}}''(s_v)>0$; the radial potential Hessian for $H=(0,r/\sqrt2)^T$ at $r=v$ is then $v^2V_{\mathrm{ret}}''(s_v)>0$, while gauge-orbit directions need not have positive Hessian. Degenerate local minima remain permitted under the local-minimum condition itself. For the displayed cubic potential the stationarity and nondegeneracy conditions read
$$-\mu_H^2+\lambda v^2-\frac{3C_Hv^4}{4\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}=0,\qquad 2\lambda-\frac{3C_Hv^2}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}>0.$$
No minimum or stationarity condition is imposed on $V_4$ separately: retained higher-dimension terms may shift or supply the local minimum. Without the full-potential assumption $v$ is only a reference value. No global stability, large-field behavior, or control of omitted higher-dimension terms is inferred from a minimum of the truncated potential.

This is an operator-level model on smooth fields and compactly supported variations; total divergences are therefore zero in the associated action comparison. Its low-energy use is restricted to external momenta small compared with $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$, with the finite dimension-six truncation understood formally and without a numerical remainder bound. No regulator or functional measure is adopted, and no finite graph cutoff is identified with $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$. The postulate asserts no path integral, continuum limit, ultraviolet completion, or empirical realization.

items.title: Nonlinear electroweak Goldstone and scalar-singlet EFT data
items.design_state: Adopts the nonlinear SU(2)-valued Goldstone field and independent scalar singlet with the exact right hypercharge action and separate HEFT scales.
items.statement:
Use the same four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, direct-product global gauge group, gauge connection, fermion representations, family content, and the preceding model's exact baryon- and lepton-number selection rules on formal local interactions. No anomaly-free quantum-current claim is made. In particular, the hypercharge-one-half Higgs doublet of that model is replaced in this realization by three angular Goldstone coordinates and a real scalar singlet; this is a distinct adopted model interface, not a deduction that the two models have identical field spaces.

Let $J=(-v,\infty)$, where $v>0$ is the mass-one reference radius from the preceding model. A scalar field is a smooth map $h:M\to J$ and is invariant under the electroweak gauge group. The Goldstone field is a smooth map $U:M\to SU(2)$, with $SU(2)$ represented by its defining $2\times2$ unitary matrices of determinant one. For smooth gauge transformations $g_L:M\to SU(2)_L$ and $z:M\to U(1)_Y$, set
$$g_R(z)=\operatorname{diag}(z^3,z^{-3}),\qquad U(x)\longmapsto g_L(x)U(x)g_R(z(x))^{-1},\qquad h(x)\longmapsto h(x).$$
Thus the left factor is the linearly represented $SU(2)_L$ gauge action, the right factor is the embedded hypercharge action, and $h$ is a gauge singlet. For explicitness, take
$$\sigma^1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma^2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma^3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad T_a=\frac{\sigma^a}{2}.$$
The exponential chart
$$U(\pi)=\exp\!\left(\frac{2i\pi^aT_a}{v}\right),\qquad \pi\in\mathbb R^3,\quad \|\pi\|<\pi v,$$
is a smooth coordinate chart near the identity; $U$ itself is the globally valued group field and is not identified with one global exponential-coordinate chart.

Write $W_\mu=W_\mu^aT_a$ and use the local covariant derivative
$$D_\mu U=\partial_\mu U+i g W_\mu U-i g' B_\mu U T_3,$$
with dimensionless gauge couplings $g,g'$ and the same right-principal connection convention as the shared gauge data. The adopted two-derivative scalar density is
$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{scalar}}^{(2)}=-\frac12K(h)\,\partial_\mu h\,\partial^\mu h-\frac{v^2}{4}F_C(h)\operatorname{Tr}\!\left((D_\mu U)^\dagger D^\mu U\right)-V(h),$$
where $K$ and $F_C$ are supplied smooth real dimensionless functions on $J$, $K(h)>0$ and $F_C(h)>0$ on the field range used, $K(0)=F_C(0)=1$, and $V$ is a supplied real smooth potential of mass dimension four with $V'(0)=0$. Higher local interactions may use smooth coefficient functions of $h/v$, the same gauge and matter fields, covariant derivatives, and curvature tensors, with B and L conserved. This statement adopts no finite derivative or chiral truncation; the separate power-counting definition specifies those cutoffs.

The assigned mass dimensions are $[h]=[\pi^a]=[v]=[\Lambda_{\mathrm{HEFT}}]=[\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}]=1$, $[U]=[g]=[g']=[K]=[F_C]=0$, and $[W_\mu]=[B_\mu]=1$; the potential $V$ has dimension four, $\partial_\mu$ has dimension one, and any separately supplied regulator cutoff has dimension one. Thus the exponent defining $U(\pi)$ is dimensionless and every term in $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{scalar}}^{(2)}$ has dimension four. The independent HEFT cutoff $\Lambda_{\mathrm{HEFT}}>0$, the radius $v$, the SMEFT coefficient scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$, and any finite-regulator cutoff are separate data; no equality or hierarchy among them is imposed here. Its low-energy use assumes external momenta small compared with $\Lambda_{\mathrm{HEFT}}$; this is an applicability condition and supplies no numerical remainder bound. It adopts no functional measure or regulator and implies no path integral, ultraviolet completion, infinite-volume limit, or empirical realization.

items.title: Finite dimension-six Warsaw coefficient contract
items.design_state: Defines the source-listed B- and L-conserving dimension-six Warsaw coefficient representatives and their family and conjugation conventions without claiming a local classification proof.
items.statement:
Use the fields, direct-product gauge group, hypercharge normalization, three-family content, exact $U(1)_B\times U(1)_L$ symmetries, natural units and coefficient scale of the preceding linearly realized model. A local operator is a finite polynomial in these fields and their covariant derivatives at one spacetime point, with all Lorentz, gauge and family indices contracted to a Lorentz and gauge scalar. Its canonical dimension assigns one to $H$ and each derivative, $3/2$ to a fermion, and two to a field strength.

The **Warsaw coefficient contract** is the finite dimension-six source list of gauge-invariant representatives $Q_i^{(6)}$ in Tables 2 and 3 of Grzadkowski, Iskrzynski, Misiak and Rosiek (2010), under their stated field, hypercharge, Lorentz, color and $SU(2)_L$ conventions, with exact baryon- and lepton-number conservation. The list consists of the source's 15 bosonic, 19 single-fermion-current and 25 four-fermion structures before family multiplicities and Hermitian conjugates; it is not a count of independent three-family complex coefficients. Include all family-index components for three generations, with the source's stated permutation, Hermiticity and conjugation rules; impose no family-universality or diagonal-flavor restriction. No right-handed neutrino field or dimension-five Weinberg operator is included.

In particular, this contract includes the source representative $Q_{H\Box}=(H^\dagger H)\Box(H^\dagger H)$, with $\Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$ and the mostly-plus metric of the adopted model. It has canonical dimension six because each Higgs field has dimension one and $\Box$ has dimension two.

For $Q_i^{(6)}$ use the dimensionless Wilson coefficient convention
$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{dim}\,6}=\frac{1}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}\sum_i C_i Q_i^{(6)},\qquad \Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0,$$
with the coefficient tensors chosen so the density is real after the required Hermitian conjugates are added. The retained operator contract has derivative-jet order at most two, maximum field degree six, canonical dimension at most six, and loop order zero. Compactly supported field variations make total divergences vanish in action-level uses.

The source's complete-basis assertion is adopted as a literature-defined coefficient list, not proved by this item. The separate finite invariant-operator quotient supplies only its declared complex-algebraic selection. In this contract that quotient is explicitly formal: no equality between its algebraic invariant space and the full physical compact-gauge invariant space, and no local proof of the EOM/IBP/Fierz classification, is claimed. The finite-cutoff quotient does not add a full Axiom of Choice assumption to the field-data suppliers' stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ base.

items.title: Finite electroweak HEFT chiral and loop counting
items.design_state: Defines the source-convention HEFT chiral and loop grading and finite NLO classes separately from canonical-dimension counting.
items.statement:
Use the HEFT fields $U$, $h$, gauge curvatures, fermions and smooth coefficient functions of $h/v$ from the preceding HEFT model. Since $h/v\in(-1,\infty)$ there, a coefficient function is a specified smooth map $F:(-1,\infty)\to\mathbb C$, with conjugation conditions chosen so the retained density is real. The canonical engineering dimension $\Delta$ is the mass weight of the local polynomial in fields and derivatives; it is the weight supplied by the finite-jet operator definition. The **chiral/loop count** is separate data and is not inferred from $\Delta$.

Adopt the electroweak chiral loop convention of Buchalla, Catà and Krause. A **finite connected diagram for this count** is a finite multigraph with nonempty vertex set $\mathcal V_\Gamma$, internal edge set $\mathcal E_\Gamma$, and finitely many labelled external half-edges attached to its vertices, such that the graph on $\mathcal V_\Gamma$ is connected. Parallel internal edges and loops are allowed; each internal edge joins compatible field half-edges. Every vertex has one of the source-convention labels below, with the indicated field half-edges. Define its loop number by
$$L:=|\mathcal E_\Gamma|-|\mathcal V_\Gamma|+1\in\mathbb N_0.$$
Thus $L$ is the first Betti number of the connected graph. The external half-edges are counted by $F_L$ left-handed fermions and their conjugates, $F_R$ right-handed fermions and their conjugates, $V$ gauge bosons, $B$ Goldstone bosons, and $H_{\mathrm{ext}}$ scalar singlets. The source-convention vertex counts are nonnegative integers: $\nu_k$ counts Yukawa vertices with two opposite-chirality fermion half-edges and $k$ Goldstone half-edges but no singlet-$h$ half-edge; $m_l$ counts gauge-Goldstone vertices with one gauge and $l$ Goldstone half-edges; $r_s$ counts vertices with two gauge and $s$ Goldstone half-edges; $x$ and $u$ count, respectively, vertices with four and three gauge half-edges; $z_L,z_R$ count vertices with one gauge half-edge and two left- or right-handed fermion half-edges; $\tau_{tb}$ counts singlet-dependent Yukawa vertices with two opposite-chirality fermion half-edges, $t$ Goldstone half-edges, and $b\geq1$ singlet-$h$ half-edges; and $\omega_q$ counts scalar-potential vertices with $q\geq2$ singlet-$h$ half-edges. Here $k,l,s,t\in\mathbb N_0$, $b\in\mathbb N$, and $q\in\mathbb N$ with $q\geq2$. The leading two-derivative scalar sector also has vertices with $2j$ Goldstone and $a$ singlet half-edges, $j,a\in\mathbb N_0$ and $(j,a)\ne(0,0)$; their counts do not enter the degree formula. These labels specify only the valence data used by the source counting convention. Set
$$\nu=\sum_k\nu_k+\sum_{t,b}\tau_{tb},\qquad m=\sum_lm_l,\qquad r=\sum_sr_s,\qquad z=z_L+z_R,\qquad \omega=\sum_q\omega_q.$$
For these counts the source chiral degree of the external-momentum factor is
$$d_\chi=2L+2-\frac{F_L+F_R}{2}-V-\nu-m-2r-2x-u-z-2\omega.$$
Here $p$ denotes the common external-momentum scale in the source power-counting expression, and $d_\chi$ is the exponent of its $p^{d_\chi}$ factor; the condition $d_\chi\geq0$ is the source-defined formal counterterm-counting filter.
The factors $(\varphi/v)^B$ and $(h/v)^{H_{\mathrm{ext}}}$ contain the external Goldstone and singlet fields and do not increase $d_\chi$. Vertices $\varphi^{2j}h^a$ from the leading two-derivative scalar sector likewise carry no additional term in this degree formula. Here $\varphi=(\varphi^1,\varphi^2,\varphi^3)$ is the local Goldstone coordinate in the chart $\|\varphi\|<\pi v$ defined by $U=\exp(2i\varphi^aT_a/v)$, with $T_a=\sigma^a/2$ as in the adopted HEFT model. The chiral cutoff and loop cutoff are supplied independently; this contract retains the leading order and the one-loop next-to-leading counterterm classes with $L\leq1$ and $d_\chi\geq0$.

The source's six schematic next-to-leading structural families are $UhD^4$, $X^2Uh$, $XUhD^2$, $\psi^2UhD$, $\psi^2UhD^2$, and $\psi^4Uh$. Here $Uh$ denotes an arbitrary finite product of $U,U^\dagger,h$ factors, $X_{\mu\nu}$ is a gauge-curvature factor, $D$ is a covariant-derivative factor, and $\psi$ is a spinor-field factor; superscripts count the indicated factors. Each displayed monomial is understood with its Lorentz and gauge indices contracted to an invariant scalar and may be multiplied by its own smooth function of $h/v$. These are six structural families, not six finite lists of operators; the smooth-function dependence is not Taylor-truncated here. No class list or operator-level coefficient relation from a finite canonical-dimension SMEFT basis is identified with this full HEFT list.

The scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{HEFT}}>0$ controlling the derivative expansion and the symmetry-breaking scale $v>0$ are separate supplied mass scales. A condition such as external momentum small compared with $\Lambda_{\mathrm{HEFT}}$ is an applicability assumption only. Chiral order and loop order are formal organizing labels, not convergence claims or numerical bounds on omitted terms.

items.title: The selected SMEFT model is a restricted HEFT branch
items.design_state: Proves the smooth equivariant nonzero-doublet patch map and the finite polynomial and coefficient-image restrictions of the selected SMEFT branch.
items.statement:
Let $v>0$, let $J=(-v,\infty)$, and use the linearly transforming complex doublet $H$ with hypercharge $Y=1/2$ and the nonlinear fields $h\in J$, $U\in SU(2)$, with the gauge transformations and mostly-plus Minkowski conventions of the two adopted electroweak models. Here $\sigma^2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$ is the second Pauli matrix. Put $e_2=(0,1)^T$, $\widetilde H=i\sigma^2H^*$, and define
$$\Phi:J\times SU(2)\longrightarrow\mathbb C^2\setminus\{0\},\qquad \Phi(h,U)=\frac{v+h}{\sqrt2}Ue_2.$$
Then $\Phi$ is a smooth diffeomorphism onto the nonzero-doublet field space. Its inverse is obtained from $\rho=(H^\dagger H)^{1/2}>0$ and $\Sigma(H)=(\widetilde H,H)$ by
$$h=\sqrt2\rho-v,\qquad U=\frac{\Sigma(H)}{\rho}.$$
It is equivariant for $SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$: for $g_L\in SU(2)_L$ and $z\in U(1)_Y$, under $H\mapsto g_Lz^3H$ one has $U\mapsto g_LU\operatorname{diag}(z^3,z^{-3})^{-1}$ and $h\mapsto h$. The point $H=0$ is excluded; no value of $U$ is assigned there.

For the finite selected SMEFT interaction consisting of the renormalizable terms and the source-defined Warsaw representatives through canonical dimension six, substitute $H=\Phi(h,U)$ and its conjugate into each representative and expand covariant derivatives by the product rule. In the unnormalized radial variable $x=h/v$, every resulting coefficient function multiplying a fixed finite HEFT derivative/Goldstone monomial is a polynomial in $x$ of degree at most six. More precisely, after choosing a finite ordered list of the resulting HEFT monomials and a common dimensionally consistent coefficient normalization, the HEFT coefficient tuple is $f=R c$, where $c$ is the finite selected SMEFT coefficient tuple and $R$ is the finite matrix defined by this substitution. Thus its functions and coefficients obey the polynomial and linear-image correlations of this selected branch; they are not freely specifiable smooth HEFT functions. For example, an independent coefficient function $e^x$ is not in the degree-at-most-six polynomial class on any open interval. These radial functions are analytic in $h/v$ before any further field reparametrization.

The canonical-dimension cutoff and the separately defined HEFT chiral/loop grading remain distinct: the substitution does not identify all HEFT classes through a chosen chiral order with the Warsaw list. The result is a conditional statement about the named finite coefficient representatives and their local field substitution, not a proof that a formal algebraic invariant quotient equals the full physical compact-gauge invariant space. It asserts neither that every HEFT lies on this branch nor that every HEFT point has a weakly coupled ultraviolet completion.

items.title: Tree-level scalar normalization and the charged-vector coupling
items.design_state: Computes the local Q_HBox scalar kinetic coefficient and charged-vector coupling under the stated positivity and boundary assumptions.
items.statement:
Use the selected mostly-plus, four-dimensional electroweak model with $v>0$, dimensionless gauge coupling $g>0$, and coefficient scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0$. Choose a real dimensionless coefficient $C_{H\Box}$, set all other dimension-six coefficients to zero, and retain
$$Q_{H\Box}=(H^\dagger H)\Box(H^\dagger H),\qquad \Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu,$$
with Lagrangian contribution $C_{H\Box}Q_{H\Box}/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2$. On the nonzero-doublet patch choose the local gauge transformation $g_L(x)=U(x)^{-1}$ and $z(x)=1$, which sets $U=I$ and gives $H=(0,(v+h)/\sqrt2)^T$. Impose compact support or boundary conditions that make the surface term in the action vanish.

The quadratic scalar coefficient after integration by parts is
$$K(h)=1+\frac{2C_{H\Box}(v+h)^2}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}.$$
If
$$K(0)=1+\frac{2C_{H\Box}v^2}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}>0,$$
then $K$ is positive on some open interval about $h=0$. In that interval define the locally canonical radial coordinate $\widehat h(h)=\int_0^h\sqrt{K(s)}\,ds$. Define $W_\mu^\pm=(W_\mu^1\mp iW_\mu^2)/\sqrt2$ and define $m_W^2(h)$ as the coefficient in the vector mass term $-m_W^2(h)W_\mu^+W^{-\mu}$. The charged-vector mass parameter and its dimensionless linear coupling in this coordinate are
$$m_W^2(h)=\frac{g^2(v+h)^2}{4},\qquad \kappa_W:=\left.\frac{v}{2m_W^2(0)}\frac{dm_W^2}{d\widehat h}\right|_{h=0}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+2C_{H\Box}v^2/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2}}.$$
These are conditional tree-level coefficient predictions of this selected local action. Interpret $h=0$ as a vacuum only when the full retained scalar potential $V_{\mathrm{ret}}(s)$, with $s=H^\dagger H$, has a local minimum at $s=v^2/2$ in the selected EFT field range. At this coefficient point every other dimension-six coefficient, including $C_H$, is zero and $Q_{H\Box}$ vanishes on constant fields, so $V_{\mathrm{ret}}=V_4$ here. This is an optional condition on the supplied potential parameters; otherwise these are coefficients at the reference configuration. No measured value, coefficient fit, loop correction, discarded-order bound, or general HEFT relation is asserted.
